article_title: Selecting graduates for the interns' award by using multisource feedback process: does it work?
citation: Strachan Kathryn, Otoom Sameer, AL-Gallaf Amal, Al Ansari Ahmed. (2017). Selecting graduates for the interns' award by using multisource feedback process: does it work? BMC Research Notes. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13104-017-2848-6
title: BDF/PCC instrument: a 39-item multisource feedback questionnaire for professionalism, communication, and collaboration
description: The Bahrain Defence Force Instrument for professionalism, communication, and collaboration (BDF/PCC) is a multisource feedback questionnaire built from prior instruments including PAR, MAAS-Global, the Calgary-Cambridge tool, SPRAT, AITCS, and specialist opinions. "It included 39 items, 15 of which measured professionalism, 13 of which to measured communication skills, and 11 of which measured collaboration." It uses a 5-point response scale from "among the worst" to "among the best", with an "unable to assess" option.
requirements: Designed so that various groups, such as interns, consultants, senior medical colleagues, and coworkers, could all use it; raters needed to have spent at least 1 or 2 months working alongside the graduate.
constraints: The authors state the study's low response rates mean the MSF process using this instrument is not feasible as currently implemented.
target_learners: medical graduates (interns) assessed by physicians, nurses, and fellow students
examples: Ratings on the instrument's 5-point scale were averaged across observers for each candidate; the top candidate scored 4.77 out of 5 overall.
